content: {"entries":[{"revises":[],"knowledge":[{"text":"Under the initial Skill installation (parent null), the added hold-transform guidance directed heating/cooling by picking up the object and applying `heat`/`cool` with the appliance while holding it, rather than placing it inside and toggling the door. In the paired heat-egg task, Q9 took egg1, opened the microwave while holding it, applied `heat egg 1 with microwave 1`, then moved egg1 to countertop1 for a 9-step success; P9 instead moved egg1 into the microwave and then repeatedly opened/closed the door without heating and ended at the 50-step limit. Q8 also heated held apple1 with a closed microwave and completed an 8-step success, while P8 opened the microwave first and took 14 steps. Q4 cooled held bread1 with a closed fridge and succeeded in 8 steps. These cases support that the hold-transform approach can work without door toggling and can be efficient, but the joint installation and tasks where no target was acquired prevent attributing all outcomes to this clause alone.","evidence":["diff","Q9:4","Q9:6","Q9:7","Q9:8","Q9:9","P9:11","P9:14","P9:15","P9:16","P9:50","Q8:4","Q8:5","Q8:8","P8:11","P8:12","P8:14","Q4:3","Q4:5","Q4:6","Q4:8"]},{"text":"Acquired-target clean/transform-then-place sequences were preserved in every successful current candidate run. Q1 cleaned spoon1 with sinkbasin1 and moved it to diningtable1 (10 steps; parent P1 did the same in 9 and had no extra initial countertop check). Q3 and Q4 cooled bread1 with fridge1 and moved it to countertop1, Q8 heated apple1 with microwave1 and moved it to fridge1, and Q9 heated egg1 with microwave1 and moved it to countertop1. No successful candidate was observed abandoning an acquired target before the required placement. This supports preservation of the sequence when acquisition succeeds, but does not show that the search or recovery clauses caused the successes.","evidence":["diff","Q1:7","Q1:8","Q1:9","Q1:10","P1:7","P1:8","P1:9","Q3:5","Q3:7","Q3:8","Q3:9","Q4:4","Q4:6","Q4:8","Q8:3","Q8:5","Q8:8","Q9:4","Q9:7","Q9:9"]},{"text":"Search and recovery guidance did not ensure coverage of candidate locations: in cool-plate P6/Q6, P6 succeeded in 43 steps after opening cabinet9, taking plate1, cooling it with fridge1, and moving it to diningtable1, while Q6 hit the 50-step limit after cycling among countertop1/2, cabinet1/2/3, drawer1/2, and diningtable1 without opening cabinet9. In cool-pot P7/Q7, P7 succeeded in 20 steps using pot2 from stoveburner4, cooling it with fridge1, and moving it to countertop1, while Q7 hit the 50-step limit, acquiring pot2 only at Q7:49 and then going to fridge1 at Q7:50 without cooling or placing it. In heat-mug P10/Q10, both failed, but Q10 never reached countertop3 where P10 found mug4; in P2/Q2 both failed without acquiring bread. Candidate Q4 did find bread quickly and succeed, so the search shortcomings are task-dependent rather than universal.","evidence":["diff","P6:37","P6:38","P6:40","P6:43","Q6:1","Q6:17","Q6:23","Q6:31","Q6:50","P7:16","P7:18","P7:19","P7:20","Q7:49","Q7:50","P10:41","P10:42","Q10:25","Q10:50","P2:50","Q2:50","Q4:3","Q4:4","Q4:8"]},{"text":"Task-noun object selection was not consistently followed when similar objects were present. In heat-mug P10/Q10, parent P10 eventually took the required mug4 from countertop3, whereas candidate Q10 took cup1 from cabinet8 at Q10:25, examined and heated cup1 at Q10:35/Q10:39, and never acquired mug4 before the step limit; after heating cup1 it went to coffeemachine1 but did not place it, then repeated heating cup1 at Q10:44 and still did not place it. In cool-pot P7/Q7, candidate Q7 first took pan1 from stoveburner2 at Q7:7 and moved it to stoveburner1 at Q7:8, only taking pot2 at Q7:49; parent P7 also initially took pan1 at P7:4 but recovered by taking pot2 at P7:16 and succeeded. In cool-pan P5/Q5, both failed at 50 steps; Q5 did not take visible pot1, so it is unclear whether a required pan existed. These current pairs show wrong-type selection and failure to recover to the named object, but they do not establish that the guidance was uniformly ignored.","evidence":["diff","P10:41","P10:42","Q10:25","Q10:35","Q10:39","Q10:40","Q10:44","Q10:45","Q10:50","P7:4","P7:16","P7:20","Q7:7","Q7:8","Q7:49","P5:28","P5:50","Q5:5","Q5:50"]},{"text":"Action-format guidance coincided with cleaner commands in many candidate runs but did not eliminate non-admissible targets. Candidate Q8:5 and Q9:7 used exact admissible heat commands, and Q1, Q3, and Q4 completed successful sequences with admissible actions; parent baselines still contained empty/reasoning actions such as P2:1, P2:2, P2:6 and P5:5. However Q6 still used 'go to cabinet 3' when it was not admissible at Q6:6, Q6:23, Q6:29, Q6:35, Q6:40, and Q6:47; Q7 used 'go to stoveburner 2' when it was not admissible at Q7:17 and Q7:46; and Q10 recorded a missing_action_tag fallback at Q10:33. Thus the clause is associated with cleaner output in several runs but did not guarantee legal targets or formatting.","evidence":["diff","Q8:5","Q9:7","Q1:10","Q3:9","Q4:8","P2:1","P2:2","P2:6","P5:5","Q6:6","Q6:23","Q6:29","Q6:35","Q6:40","Q6:47","Q7:17","Q7:46","Q10:33"]}]}]}
